candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L, respectively, for Cyanide.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes proposed numeric cyanide limits (daily max and monthly average). A different reading of which limit type applies to a given monitoring period or whether these proposed limits are operative for FY2025 would change which enforceable numeric limit is used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall have a 1-year compliance schedule to achieve final limitations for Cyanide pollutant. The permit will require compliance schedule reports.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A 1-year compliance schedule to achieve final limitations implies interim enforceability may differ from final limits; compliance schedule reports are an additional obligation. Interpretation of whether FY2025 falls within the schedule period, whether interim limits apply, and how missing cyanide results during the schedule should be classified could change limit applicability (A), reporting/monitoring obligations (B), and missing-evidence semantics (C).

candidates.exact_span: Technology based pollutants; BOD5 and TSS, are proposed to be monitored five times per week, with sampling on at least five different days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies monitoring frequency and day-distribution requirements for BOD5 and TSS. Different interpretation of 'five times per week' or 'at least five different days' could change whether monitoring was required for a given week or period in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored continuously using a totalizing meter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes continuous flow monitoring using a totalizing meter. Whether continuous metering was required versus periodic sampling affects monitoring-obligation evaluation for flow in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sample type for BOD5 and TSS is 12-Hr composite.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines required sample type for BOD5 and TSS monitoring. A different interpretation of composite sampling requirements could change whether reported samples satisfy applicable monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The monitoring frequencies of daily for TRC and five times per week for E. coli, pH and flow are consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets or incorporates monitoring frequencies for TRC (daily) and E. coli, pH, and flow (five times per week). Interpretation of whether FY2025 obligations follow these stated frequencies or only 'consistent' prior-permit terms could change required-monitoring determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Report requirements of once per week for TDS is also consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Characterizes TDS as a reporting requirement rather than a stated numeric discharge limit. Whether TDS is report-only versus subject to an enforceable numeric limit affects compliance comparison (A) and the applicable monitoring/reporting obligation (B).

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will not propose any WET limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that no WET numeric limits will be proposed. Interpretation of whether WET results are subject to numeric compliance comparison versus monitoring-only affects Purpose A limit applicability.

candidates.exact_span: However, continuation of WET monitoring is proposed in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Proposes continued WET monitoring despite no WET limits. Whether WET testing remained a required monitoring obligation in FY2025 depends on interpreting continuation of monitoring under the draft permit.

candidates.exact_span: Previously it was shown that the CD was 2.34%. When the critical dilution is equal to or less than 10%, in lieu of the 7-day chronic test, a 48-hour acute test may be run using a 10:1 acute to chronic ratio; 23.4% rounded to the nearest whole number 23%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Critical dilution of 2.34% triggers substitution of 48-hour acute testing for 7-day chronic testing and determines the 23% dilution used in acute testing. Different interpretation of CD value, the ≤10% threshold, or the acute-to-chronic ratio calculation could change which WET test type and dilution series were required.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall conduct a 48-hour acute test using Daphnia pulex once per quarter, and a 48-hour acute test using Pimephales promelas once per quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes species-specific WET acute test obligations at quarterly frequency. Interpretation of quarterly scheduling within FY2025 could change whether monitoring was required for each quarter and species.

candidates.exact_span: After the first four quarters without failures, the permittee may apply for a frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional reduction pathway after four failure-free quarters. Whether FY2025 quarters count toward the four-quarter threshold, and whether an approved reduction eliminates otherwise-expected WET monitoring, affects monitoring-obligation evaluation (B) and classification of missing WET evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any failure afterwards shall re-establish all tests for both species to once per quarter for the remainder of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Failure-triggered reinstatement of quarterly testing for both species. Interpretation of what constitutes a failure and when reinstatement applies could change required monitoring frequency (B) and whether absent WET results represent missing required evidence versus a period where reduced monitoring was permitted (C).

candidates.exact_span: The test series will be 10%, 13%, 17%, 23% and 31%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the dilution series for WET acute testing. Different interpretation of required dilution percentages could change whether conducted tests satisfied monitoring requirements.
